en: Although many think Manila is the largest, Davao City is actually the largest city in the Philippines by land area.
Contrary to the belief that it has a flat top, Mayon Volcano is famous for its perfectly symmetrical conical shape.
Despite common tropical misconceptions, the equator does not cross the Philippines, as the entire country is located north of the equator.
While often thought to live only in Mindanao, the Philippine eagle also inhabits the Sierra Madre mountains in Luzon and the island of Leyte.
People mistakenly assume Taal Volcano sits on the mainland, but it is actually located on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake.
Despite its name containing the Spanish word for sea, Laguna de Bay is actually the largest freshwater lake in the Philippines.
Many confuse it as the national capital, but Baguio City is officially just the summer capital, while Manila remains the national capital.
Although its name suggests otherwise, the Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the archipelago, not the western side.
Travelers often mistakenly group Palawan with the Visayas, but it is administratively part of the Mimaropa region in the Luzon group.
Some incorrectly claim Mount Pulag is the highest peak, but Mount Apo in Mindanao holds the title of the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Tourists often confuse its location with Cebu, but the famous Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park is actually located in Palawan.
Visitors might assume it is near the coast, but the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is situated in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
